chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qāsim ibn Sulaymān, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a slave, if he falsely accuses a free person, how many lashes is he to receive? He said: “Forty.” And he said: “If he commits an indecency, then upon him is half the punishment.”

So this is an anomalous report, contrary to the apparent meaning of the Qur'an and to the many reports that we have cited earlier. Whatever is of this kind is not acted upon, nor is something like it used as an objection.
As for its contradicting the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, that is because Allah, Exalted is He, said:
“And those who accuse chaste women…” up to His saying: “Then flog them with eighty lashes, and do not ever accept their testimony.”
And that is general regarding every slanderer, whether free or a slave.
As for His, Exalted is He, saying:
“Then if they commit an indecency, upon them is half of what is upon the chaste women of the punishment,”
then that is specifically restricted to zinā, based on what we have explained from the reports, and because it is not permissible for them to contradict one another.

key_terms.افْتَرَى: falsely accused or fabricated a slanderous charge
key_terms.الزِّنَى: illicit sexual intercourse, to which the half-punishment verse is restricted here
key_terms.الْعَبْدِ: the slave; the legally unfree person under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.الْقُرْآنِ: the Qur'an, cited as the primary textual proof
key_terms.ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً: eighty lashes; the Qur'anic hadd punishment for false accusation
key_terms.خَبَرٌ شَاذٌّ: an anomalous report that conflicts with stronger evidence
key_terms.فَاحِشَةٍ: an indecency; here cited in the Qur'anic legal context
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ: is flogged; receives lashes as a legal punishment

ai.seo_question: Does the punishment for false accusation differ for a slave and a free person in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal ruling concerning a slave who commits false accusation and presents a report stating that the punishment is forty lashes. The author then rejects that report as anomalous because it conflicts with the apparent meaning of the Qur'an and numerous other narrations, arguing that the Qur'anic rule of eighty lashes for slander is general, while the verse about half the punishment applies specifically to zinā.
